chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, all from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you leave your house intending Hajj and 'Umrah, if God wills, supplicate with the Supplication of Relief, which is: 'There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god but Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and Lord of the Magnificent Throne. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

Then say: 'O Allah, be for me a Protector from every stubborn tyrant and from every rebellious Satan.' Then say: 'In the Name of Allah I enter, and in the Name of Allah I go out, and in the Way of Allah.' O Allah, I proceed before my forgetfulness and my haste with 'In the Name of Allah and whatever Allah wills.' In this journey of mine, I remember it or forget it. O Allah, You are the One sought for help in all affairs, and You are the Companion in the journey and the Caliph (Caretaker) for the family.

O Allah, ease for us our journey, and fold the earth for us, and make us travel in it with Your obedience and the obedience of Your Messenger. O Allah, rectify our backs, and bless us in what You have provided for us, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the fatigue of travel, and the anguish of the return, and the evil of the view of the family, wealth, and children. O Allah, You are my reinforcement and my helper. With You I disembark and with You I travel.

O Allah, I ask You in this journey of mine for joy and for doing that which pleases You regarding me. O Allah, cut off from me its distance and its hardship, and be my companion in it, and replace me with goodness for my family. And there is no might and no strength except with Allah.

O Allah, I am Your servant, and this is Your carrier, and the direction is Your direction, and the journey is to You, and You have looked upon what no one else has looked upon. So make this journey of mine an expiation for what preceded it of my sins, and be a helper for me upon it, and suffice me from its fatigue and its hardship, and teach me from the words and deeds that which brings Your pleasure, for indeed I am Your servant, and with You, and for You.

So when you put your foot in the stirrup, say: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. In the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest.' So when you are established upon your mount, and your load is established with you, say: 'Praise be to Allah who guided us to Islam, and taught us the Quran, and favored us with Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). Glory be to Allah. Glory be to Him who made this subservient to us, and we were not able to do it. And indeed to our Lord we must return. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

O Allah, You are the Carrier upon the back, and the One sought for help in the affair. O Allah, bring us to a destination that reaches to goodness, a destination that reaches to Your forgiveness and Your pleasure. O Allah, there is no traversing except Your traversing, and there is no goodness except Your goodness, and there is no Protector other than You.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and phrases to recite when leaving home for Hajj or travel?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a structured liturgy for departure, blending the *Dua al-Faraj* with specific verses to sanctify the journey as an act of worship. It emphasizes spiritual preparedness by seeking divine protection from arrogance and Shaytan, while framing travel as a means for sin expiation and spiritual elevation. This practice reflects the Shia tradition of integrating Quranic recitation with supplication to transform physical movement into a continuous state of dhikr.
